problem_summary.summary: Reverse each consecutive group of k nodes, preserving the order of any final group shorter than k.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: possibly-null ListNode head and positive integer k. Return the modified head without changing node values. The judge supplies ListNode { int val; ListNode next; }.
constraints: Any incomplete final group remains unchanged

brute_force.explanation: Collect node references, reverse each complete k-sized interval in the array, and reconnect the sequence. Incomplete tail references remain in their original order.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Each complete array block is replaced by its exact reverse, while the final short block is untouched. Reconnecting adjacent references implements precisely that ordering on the original nodes.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — every node is collected and each complete group's references are reversed once.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the node-reference array.

optimized.explanation: Use a dummy predecessor. Before reversing a group, scan ahead k nodes; if the group is complete, reverse its links in place and connect its new head and tail to neighboring groups.
optimized.correctness_idea: The look-ahead prevents any partial suffix from being touched. Reversing exactly the k links swaps that group's endpoints while preserving every node, and reconnecting the saved boundaries maintains one list.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — look-ahead and reversal together process each node a constant number of times.

steps.action: Reverse 1 and 3, then connect dummy to 3 and 1 to 5.

steps.condition: Two nodes are available after node 1.
steps.action: Reverse 5 and 7; node 1 links to 7 and node 5 links to 9.

edge_cases.handling: Each group contains one node, so all links remain in the same order.

edge_cases.case: List length is not divisible by k
edge_cases.handling: The incomplete suffix is detected before mutation and stays unchanged.
The dummy's next is null and null is returned.
